2. Fixed Income EJV Schema 
Overview and Usage Notes 
Pricing End-of-Day (VPD) 
We provide end-of-day pricing information, including trade date, pricing source, price, yield, and pricing method. 
This is a value-added service defined as the ‘best’ collected or calculated price to derive bond yields. End-of-day 
pricing combines LSEG evaluated pricing, and LSEG composite pricing with the corresponding native and 
ISMA/Corp yields according to the hierarchy described in the section End-of-Day (EOD) Pricing. End-of-day 
pricing forms the basis for Price History. 
End-of-Day (EOD) Pricing 
This pricing is a value-added service defined as the ‘best’ collected or calculated price to derive bond yields. This 
pricing combines LSEG evaluated pricing, LSEG composite pricing, and ISMA with the corresponding native and 
ISMA/Corp yields according to the hierarchy described below.
The pricing hierarchy and a brief description of each source is listed below:  
– LSEG Evaluated Pricing: The LSEG Evaluated Pricing Service teams' knowledge, experience, and access to 
local primary markets ensures high-quality valuations that are widely sourced, consistent, and reflect current 
trader methodologies. They apply many different quality checks and process updates and new issues 24/7. 
Coverage highlights include pricing for 1.1 million fixed income securities worldwide.  
– LSEG Composite Pricing: For a given instrument, LSEG derives a composite price from snaps of market 
closing prices from a diverse group of Brokers, Dealers, and Exchanges.  
– ISMA Pricing: The International Securities Market Association (ISMA) is the organization and trade association 
for the international securities market. It is well-known as one of the premier third-party providers of European 
terms and conditions and pricing data.

FIEJVExtcTerms: Exotic Bond Variables 
This table contains data for variables such as prices, dates, rates, and price ratio that typically can change due to 
business events, such as refixes. This view can be treated as both a schedule and a history of changes in bond 
terms.
Exotic bonds contain the following types of bonds: 
– Convertible into a Currency 
– Convertible into an Index 
– Convertible into a Basket 
– Convertible into a Money Market Rate 
– Convertible into a Spread 
– Convertible into a Swap 
– Complex Convertible 
– Convertible into a Debt of the Issuer 
– Exchangeable into a Debt of a Different (Other) Issuer 
– Exchangeable into an Equity of a Different (Other) Issuer 
– Flip-flop Bond (Convertible Between Bonds of the Same Issuer)

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
Note: Indexes are not applicable for Snowflake. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use FTSE Green Revenues data through 
LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the 
data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft 
SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with GR* are the Green Revenues 
data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for LSEG Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, and Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data 
types, and whether each field is nullable. Data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an 
int in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for LSEG Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Estimates Version 2 data 
through LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access 
to the data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. 
Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In LSEG Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table 
name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with TRE* are Estimates 
Version 2 data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016.  
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in 
index names and data types. Please note that references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of 
“–99999” or “–9999”; in these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) 
If the table contains a “0” value, the data was reported as having a “0” value.

billing, user management, and information.

Database Schema for I/B/E/S Estimates Version2  
 7 
CORPORATE 
Schema Overview and Usage Notes 
In I/B/E/S Estimates Version 2, there are three different versions of the data, provided side-by-side: 
– As-Contributed which represents the data as submitted by the broker; it is only available at the detail level. 
– Default data is consistent with respect to currency & split adjustments within a period (open vs closed), and is 
available for both detail & summary. 
– Normalized data is consistent with respect to currency & split adjustments across time, and is available for both 
detail & summary. 
Split adjustments are applied to both Default and Normalized values when they occur. 
Currency adjustments are applied to both Default and Normalized values as well, but they are applied differently 
based on the period type. 
Open periods are unreported (no actual exist), and analyst estimates are still being submitted. For open periods 
default and normalized data is in the default currency, which can be found in TREInfo. 
Closed periods have an actual reported, and analyst estimates are no longer submitted. For these periods default 
and normalized data is in the default currency, except in the following situations: 
If the actual reported currency does not match the default currency, the default data will be in the actual reported 
currency while normalized data is in the default currency. 
When the default currency changes the default data remains in the old default currency, while the normalized 
data changes to the new default currency. 
Data Concepts 
Detail vs Summary 
Detail estimates are raw estimates, recommendations, and actual acquired through collections. Detail estimates 
and recommendations are broker specific, and include information about the analyst providing the forecast. 
Summary estimates are analytics, such as mean, and they are calculated using the detail data.  
Identifiers 
The content is mastered on EstPermID which is a permanent identifier with a one-to-one relationship with the 
IBES Ticker. The EstPermID can link to OrgPermID, FilingID, InstrPermID, and QuotePermID. 
Mapping Notes 
I/B/E/S Estimates are at the quote level and structured around the EstPermID. However, there are two ways to 
map to EstPermId: directly through the quote level or down through the instrument level. Both can take you to the 
same estimates. 
To map from Quantitative Analytics SecCode to Quote Perm ID (QuotePermID), use the following mapping logic: 
– Domestic securities: SecMstrX.SecCode -> PermSecMapX.SecCode where EntType=55 and RegCode= 1 -> 
PermSecMapX.EntPermID -> TREInfo.QuotePermID 
[1- North America] 
– Global securities: GSecMstrX.SecCode -> PermSecMapX.SecCode where EntType=55 and RegCode= 0 -> 
PermSecMapX.EntPermID -> TREInfo.QuotePermID 
[0- Global] 
To map from Quantitative Analytics SecCode to Instrument Perm ID (InstrPermID), use the following mapping 
logic: 
– Domestic securities: SecMstrX.SecCode -> PermSecMapX.SecCode where EntType=49 and RegCode= 1 -> 
PermSecMapX.EntPermID -> TREInfo.InstrPermID 
[1- North America] 
– Global securities: GSecMstrX.SecCode -> PermSecMapX.SecCode where EntType=55 and RegCode= 0 -> 
PermSecMapX.EntPermID -> PermQuoteRef.QuotePermID -> PermQuoteRef.InstrPermID -> 
TREInfo.InstrPermID 
[0- Global]

Note that since there can be many quotes for each instrument, you must further specify which quote-level 
EstPermID to choose if you map through EntType 49/InstrPermID:
We suggest using vw_IBES2Mapping, a custom-built view that uses a hierarchy to select the best available 
mapping and simplify the query. If you haven’t installed the views, please contact us via one of the methods listed 
under Get Support.
select A.ID, A.Name, C.QuotePermID, C.InstrPermID, C.OrgPermID, B.EstPermID 
from vw_SecurityMasterX A 
      join vw_IBES2Mapping B 
            on B.SecCode=A.SecCode 
            and B.Typ=A.Typ 
      join TREInfo C 
            on C.EstPermID=B.EstPermID 
where A.ID in ('AAPL','@HONDA9')

16. Guidance Tables 
The guidance content offering provides forward-looking statements made by a company on its future financial 
performance.
It is available in two types: As-Reported Guidance and Comparable Guidance. 
– The As-Reported guidance is both Qualitative (Business & Industry outlook) and Quantitative (Revenue, 
EBITDA, Legal settlement, etc.) in nature. It is collected for 110 measures and includes textual data, along with 
line items from Income statement, cash flow & balance sheet, few ratios and Industry metrics. The as-reported 
guidance is provided at the Company and Segment level and is available for periods starting in 2002. 
– The Comparable Guidance is generated for 18 measures and is available as fielded data. It does not include 
any qualitative records. The comparable guidance is available for periods starting in 2006.

17. SQL Views 
The SQL Views provide simplified calls that run complex SQL code and address key data nuances and mapping 
requests in the LSEG Quantitative Analytics database, making it much easier to access data through LSEG 
Quantitative Analytics.  
Customers are able to see the underlying SQL code and modify/customize it as required, as well as being able to 
save the modified code as their proprietary code.  
The QA Support Team is available to provide training on the library structure and how to use the SQL Views. 
Contact Get Support if you would like the SQL views added to your server. 
The SQL Views were introduced in the LSEG Quantitative Analytics Release 6.32 in November 2016.

 102 
CORPORATE 
Field Type Nullable Description 
NormCurr_Desc varchar Y The description of the normalized currency. 
NormScale float Y Normalized factor necessary to reach the true estimate value (1 = no 
scale, 1000 = multiply by 1000). 
NormSplitFactor float Y Adjustment applied to convert the EstValue during normalization due to 
stock splits (divide). 
NormCurrAdj float Y Adjustment applied to EstValue during normalization due to currency 
adjustments (multiply). 
AsContribEstValue float Y Forecast value, delivered in ‘as contributed’ currency. 
AsContribCurrPermID int Y The currency in the actual document contributed by the company. 
AsContribCurr_Desc varchar Y The description of the reported currency. 
AsContribScale float Y Recommendation scale as contributed by the company, as a factor to 
reach the true estimate value (1 = no scale, 1000 = multiply by 1000). 
DocType varchar Y Type of the research document that the Estimate is sourced from. One of 
four values: Note, Document, Batch, or Manual. 
DocID varchar Y Filename of the research document in the system. 
RegionPermID int Y PermID for the region.
The descriptions are: 110172 = EMEA, 110173 = 
AMER, 110171 = ASIA. 
Region_Desc varchar Y Description of the RegionPermID field.
Example Use Case: 
--This query returns the detail estimates made by Deutsche Bank Equity Research for 
Microsoft 12 month price target. 
select aa.id, aa.name, cc.* 
from vw_SecurityMasterX aa 
join vw_IBES2Mapping bb 
 on bb.SecCode = aa.seccode 
 and bb.Typ = aa.typ 
join vw_IBES2DetHzn cc 
 on cc.EstPermID = bb.EstPermID 
 and cc.Measure = 31 --Price Target 
 and cc.PerType = 2 
 and cc.PerLength = 12 
 and cc.BrokerName = 'Deutsche Bank Equity Research' 
where aa.id = 'MSFT' 
order by cc.EffectiveDate, cc.ExpireDate, cc.ExpireOffset

vw_IBES2Mapping 
This view can be used to map from Security Master to the IBES V2 database.  
In order to pick the best mapping this view links a SecCode to its PermID record, selecting it looking in order at 
the latest ExpireDate (from TREInfo), the Source_, the latest EffectiveDate (from TREInfo) and the Rank (from 
PermSecMapX). The Source_ is a three level hierarchy for North American records where at the top there is the 
primary quote for a given instrument, at the second place the quote and at the bottom the instrument. For the rest 
of the World the Source_ is always the quote.

SecCode, RegCode, EstPermID

(CodeType = 11).

The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use I/B/E/S Point in Time data through 
LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the 
data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft 
SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, tables that begin with PIT* are I/B/E/S Point in Time 
data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016.  
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in 
index names and data types. Please note that references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle.

Growth float Yes The average annualized earnings per share growth for a company 
over the past five years. The average annualized growth in EPS for 
the past five years is calculated by measuring the slope of a least 
squares curve fit to the logarithm of the reported earnings (a log-
linear curve) and is expressed as a percent. If quarterly data are 
available, the line is fit to the last 21 observations (minimum of 11 
observations) of rolling four quarter EPS. The resultant slope is 
multiplied by four and exponentialized to obtain an annualized 
growth factor. If semi-annual data are available, the curve is fit to 
the last 11 (minimum of 6) observations of these semi-annual data. 
The resultant slope is multiplied by two and exponentialized to 
obtain an annualized growth factor. If only annual observations are 
available, the curve is fit to the last 6 annual (minimum of 3) 
observations (5 time periods) and the exponentiated slope is used 
to represent the growth factor. Zero and negative observations are 
excluded from the calculations.

1. Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the I/B/E/S data tables in LSEG Quantitative Analytics. 
Note: For information about the other LSEG Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other 
Database Schema documents posted on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page at 
MyAccount.

filename: QA Database Schema - IBES_v1.1.6.pdf
text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
— Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
— Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the table 
contents. 
— Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific information 
about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema description is 
available in the Database Schema for LSEG Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
— Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
— Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
— Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. Datatypes in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int in 
SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for LSEG Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use I/B/E/S data through LSEG. Note 
that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in these 
tables is dependent on the licenses you have. 
Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In LSEG Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table 
name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with IBG* are I/B/E/S global data 
tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016.  
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index 
names and data types. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle.

2. I/B/E/S Schema Overview 
and Usage Notes 
Adjustment Factors 
Where applicable, I/B/E/S history data is stored split adjusted as of the last Thursday before the third Friday of the 
month. I/B/E/S QFS data is stored split adjusted as of today. If you require unadjusted data, you can use adjustment 
factors to un-adjust the data.
The adjustment factor tables are: 
— IBESAdj: I/B/E/S Adjustment Factors 
— IBQSpl: I/B/E/S QFS Split Dates 
— IBQAdj: I/B/E/S QFS Cumulative Adjustment Factors 
— IBGSAdj: I/B/E/S Global Summary Adjustment Factors 
— IBGQSpl: I/B/E/S Global QFS Splits 
— IBGQAdj: I/B/E/S QFS Global Cumulative Adjustment Factors 
— AdjFctr: Vendor Supplemental Adjustments – Intra-month adjustment values are located in the AdjFctr table 
where AdjFctr.Database_ = 1 (I/B/E/S U.S. History) and AdjFctr.Database = 2 (I/B/E/S U.S. QFS). 
Detail and Summary Tables  
I/B/E/S offers summary consensus data, detail data, recommendations, and price targets. The detail tables contain 
broker-specific data, including information about the analyst who provided the forecast. The summary tables contain 
security-level data. Both the summary and detail data tables include actuals and estimates data.  
To enable apples-to-apples comparisons, I/B/E/S mean estimates only include estimates on the same accounting 
basis. Additionally, I/B/E/S uses majority rule: the basis of mean EPS estimates are determined on a company by 
company basis according to the majority of contributing analysts.

filename: QA Database Schema - IBES_v1.1.6.pdf
text:
Secondary Measure Data: IBGS2nd*, IBGD2nd*, and IBES2nd* Tables 
The IBGS2nd* and IBGD2nd* tables contain consensus and detail (respectively) secondary measures data. Some 
global companies report earnings on both a parent and consolidated basis. In these cases, I/B/E/S provides two 
different measure codes; for example, EPS and EPSPAR in which *PAR represents the parent data. To determine 
the primary basis for IBGS2nd* tables, look at the CanCurr field in IBGSHist3. To determine the primary basis for 
IBGD2nd* tables, look at the PrimaryFlag field in IBGQPrimMsr. 
The United States secondary tables, IBES2nd*, are not populated because all United States companies report  
on a consolidated basis. Therefore, there are no secondary estimates or actuals. This applies to the restated data  
as well.  
Primary data is found in the IBES*, IBGS*, IBD*, IBGD*, IBQ*, and IBGQ* tables. 
Secondary data is found in the IBGS2nd* and IBGD2nd* tables. 
Minority data based on International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is found in the IBESEst2M*, IBGSEst2M*, 
IBQEst2M*, and IBGQEst2M* tables.

Mapping Notes 
To map from SecMapX and GSecMapX to I/B/E/S data, use the following VenTypes:  
— VenType 2 maps from SecMapX to IBESInfo3 for US securities 
— VenType 3 maps from SecMapX to IBGSInfo3 for Canadian securities 
— VenType 42 maps from SecMapX to IBESInfo3/IBGSInfo3 for US & Canadian securities (the Exchange field  
in SecMapX identifies which table to use: 1 for IBESInfo3, 2 for IBGSInfo3) 
— VenType 2 maps from GSecMapX to IBGSInfo3 for global securities 
Regional File Universes 
Regional file universes are determined exclusively by the country of exchange assigned to the I/B/E/S ticker. 
Previously, I/B/E/S tickers were included in the regional files mostly according to the country of incorporation. 
The daily means logic was not adjusted and still remains as stated below; because of this daily means can differ from 
the way QFS is populated. 
— WHEN Country = 'NA' and SecType = 'S' THEN populate data in IBESUS* tables. 
— WHEN Country = 'NC' and SecType = 'S' THEN populate data in IBESINT* tables. 
— WHEN Country = 'NA' and SecType = 'D' and ExchCtry = 'NA' THEN populate data in IBESUS* tables. 
— WHEN Country = 'NA' and SecType = 'D' and ExchCtry = 'NC' THEN populate data in IBESINT* tables. 
— WHEN Country = 'NC' and SecType = 'D' and ExchCtry = 'NA' THEN populate data in IBESUS* tables. 
— WHEN Country = 'NC' and SecType = 'D' and ExchCtry = 'NC' THEN populate data in IBESINT* tables. 
— WHEN Country not in ('NA','NC') and SecType = 'S' THEN populate data in IBESINT* tables. 
— WHEN Country not in ('NA','NC') and SecType = 'A' THEN populate data in IBESUS* tables. 
— WHEN Country not in ('NA','NC') and SecType = 'D' and ExchCtry = 'NA' THEN populate data in  
IBESUS* tables.

This example shows how to join IbdStpL1 (above) with IBDEstL1 and IBESPerCode on PerType to retrieve the

select e.code, e.estdate, e.perdate, e.value_,st.perdate, st.stopdate, p.shortdesc,

join ibdstpl1 st

on p.periodtype = e.pertype

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the Interactive Data Corporation (IDC) Global Pricing data 
tables in Quantitative Analytics. 
NOTE 
For information about the other Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other Database Schema documents posted on the 
Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use IDC Global Pricing data through 
LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the 
data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft 
SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with GPRC* are IDC Global Pricing 
tables, tables beginning with PRC* are IDC United States Pricing tables, and tables beginning with CPRC* are 
IDC Canadian Pricing tables. 
Accessing Interactive Data Corporation (IDC) Documentation 
This document describes database organization within LSEG Quantitative Analytics, but it is not intended to 
replace IDC documentation. You may also want to refer to documentation provided for IDC Pricing by the 
Interactive Data Corporation. IDC data fields are described in detail in the IDC Interactive Data Pricing and 
Reference Data Reference Guide. 
If you have an IDC data license but do not have access to IDC documentation, contact IDC Customer Support at: 
http://www.ftinteractivedata.com

Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

Gprcadj: Global Pricing Adjustment Factors 
This table contains adjustment factors used to adjust daily pricing from the Gprcval table. 
Gprcdiv events (including stock dividends - paytypes 87, 88) are not reflected in Gprcadj. Only Gprccap events 
are reflected in this table.
Update Cycle: Daily 
Adjusted: Yes 
Indexes Index Fields 
pkey_Gprcadj (Clustered) Code, StartDate
Field  Type  Nullable Description 
Code  int  N Code is the primary link across all Gprc* tables. 
StartDate smalldatetime  N StartDate is the first date the adjustment is applied. 
EndDate  smalldatetime  Y EndDate is the last date the adjustment is applied. 
Rate  float  Y Rate is the rate of the capital event. 
Factor float  Y Factor is the cumulative adjustment factor over time.
Sample Query – adjusted pricing history 
The following query takes a given ID and returns the market cap history for the security: 
DECLARE @ID VARCHAR(20) 
SET @ID = '@HONDA9' -- Honda Motor
SELECT  S.ID AS ID 
 , S.NAME 
 , S.SEDOL 
 , V.DATE_ 
 , (V.CLOSE_ * A.FACTOR) AS ADJ_CLOSING_PRICE_LOCAL 
 , (V.CLOSE_ * A.FACTOR) / X.RATE AS ADJ_CLOSING_PRICE_USD 
FROM    QAI.DBO.GSECMSTRX S 
 JOIN QAI.DBO.GSECMAPX M 
  ON M.SECCODE = S.SECCODE 
  AND M.VENTYPE = 1  -- Global Pricing 
 JOIN  QAI.DBO.GPRCVAL V 
  ON  V.CODE = M.VENCODE   
 JOIN    QAI.DBO.GPRCADJ A 
  ON  A.CODE = V.CODE 
  AND V.DATE_ BETWEEN A.STARTDATE AND A.ENDDATE

SectionMarker 
SectionMarker defines available conversion data and the kind of conversion or subscription rights. SectionMarker 
can be: 
Code Description 
0 No data available 
1 Fully convertible into underlying asset 
2 Partially convertible into underlying asset 
3 Optionally partially convertible into underlying asset 
4 Security has subscription rights. 
5 Alternative subscription rights: security has choice of conversion or subscription rights 
6 Warrant 
7 Expiration: conversion, exercise, or subscription rights have expired 
8 Multiple assets: multiple conversion or subscription rights 
9 American style traded option: exercisable at any time 
A Cash conversion 
B Conditional terms: conversion/subscription terms are subject to variable factors 
C Complex terms: conversion terms are too complex to report adequately 
D Depository receipt: data relates to the underlying security of a depository receipt 
E Unit: data relates the underlying security of a bearer certificate 
F Future 
G Conversion based on the index value in FirstCashSubAmt 
H Scrip conversion with cash option 
I Warrant based on an equity basket 
J Warrant based on currency exchange rates 
K Strike price capped 
L Knock-out warrant 
M Convertible to cash on the basis shown in FirstCashSubAmt 
N European traded option: exercisable on expiration date 
P Structured/hybrid product
CnvOpMarker 
CnvOpMarker is the Conversion Opportunities Marker, which describes the number of conversion/subscription 
opportunities remaining.
CnvOpMarker can be: 
Code Description 
0 No remaining opportunities 
1 One opportunity remaining 
2 Two opportunities remaining 
3 Perpetual opportunity – no final date 
4 Multiple opportunities – no final date 
5 Compulsory conversion by issuing company 
8 Perpetual opportunity – final date 
9 Multiple opportunities – final date

GPrcQBM: Global Pricing Quote Basis Marker 
This table returns the quotation basis for a given security. The default is per share. 
Use this table to find the per-share value of a security when an exchange quotes on a basis other than per-share. 
IDC provides a security’s price as quoted at the exchange. However, some exchanges do not always quote a 
security per share. In these cases, QBM is used to find the per-share value of a security.
For example: 
Exchange’s price quotes are on different scales for different securities  
• Brazil quotes either on a per-share or per-thousand share basis. 
• Argentina quotes securities per 1 Peso of par value. 
Exchange’s prices have too many zeroes to fit in the file and have been scaled down  
• Zimbabwe quotes according to this standard.  
Exchange’s quote price is not per one share of security, but is instead quoted in relation to some other basis that 
does not impact market cap.

GPrcQBM History 
Most exchanges started on October 31, 2005 (the date GprcValA was implemented).

• Was the same from October 31, 2005 to present 
• Did not impact price 
• Was not in a QBM-intensive country (Brazil, Argentina) 
Backfill to January 1, 1995 for Brazil and other price-impacting QBMs. 
Vendor has no QBM data prior to 1995.

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the Interactive Data Corporation (IDC) North American 
Pricing data tables in Quantitative Analytics.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use IDC North American Pricing data 
through LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access 
to the data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of 
Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with GPRC* are IDC Global Pricing 
tables, tables beginning with PRC* are IDC United States Pricing tables, and tables beginning with CPRC* are 
IDC Canadian Pricing tables. 
Accessing Interactive Data Corporation (IDC) Documentation 
This document describes database organization within LSEG Quantitative Analytics, but it is not intended to 
replace IDC documentation. You may also want to refer to documentation provided for IDC Pricing by the 
Interactive Data Corporation. IDC data fields are described in detail in the IDC Interactive Data Pricing and 
Reference Data Reference Guide. 
If you have an IDC data license but do not have access to IDC documentation, contact IDC Customer Support at: 
http://www.ftinteractivedata.com

Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

This table contains daily equity composite pricing information, including the open and close prices. Use this table 
to find the value of an equity by date for a composite value. All data fields are stored in local currency.
Update Cycle: Daily 
Adjusted: No

Code  int  N Code is the primary link across all CPrc* tables.

High  real  Y High is the highest price at which a security traded on a given date. 
Low  real  Y Low is the lowest price at which a security traded on a given date. 
Close_  real  Y Close_ is the price at the close of the market. For stocks that do not trade on a 
given trading day, Close_ is an average of Bid and Ask.

specified period.

starting at 100 from the IPO date or, if the company history extends beyond the 
date the data has been stored, it is 100 from the point at which the data starts in 
the TRQA database (January 2, 1975). TotalRet takes into account price 
movement, dividends, spin-offs, and takeovers.

CAD and to convert them to USD, multiply by the CCFactor.

PRC.PRCSCCHG C ON I.CODE = C.CODE

AND (@DATE <= C.ENDDATE OR C.ENDDATE IS NULL) AND I.SECTYPE IN ('C') -- COMMON

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Index data through LSEG. Note that 
the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in these tables 
is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with IDX* are Index data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

IdxRlClsCode: Russell Daily Index Classification Codes 
In previous implementations of the Russell index schema, the Industry, Sector1, and Sector2 codes cross-
referenced the PrcCode2 table in the IDC Equities Pricing schema. In those implementations it was not possible 
to track industry or sector changes over time. This table overcomes that obstacle by providing a way to track 
industry and sector changes over time. 
The start date for the data in this table is 29 June 2009. 
To retrieve records with dates prior to 29 June 2009, you must cross-reference Industry and Sector1 as 
described here: 
– Industry cross-references with PrcCode2 where PrcCode2.Type_ = 10 and 
PrcCode2.Code = Industry 
– Sector1 cross-references with PrcCode2 where PrcCode2.Type_ = 11 and 
PrcCode2.Code = Sector1 
– Sector2 is not available for Russell Indexes 
For more information about PrcCode2, refer to the Quantitative Analytics Database Schema for IDC Pricing 
posted on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount. 
To retrieve records with start dates after 29 June 2009 and before 20 September 2020, cross-reference 
IdxRlClsCode.Code with the values for Industry, Sector1, or Sector2 from any Russell table, as described here: 
– Industry cross-references with IdxRlClsCode where IdxRlClsCode.Code = concatenation of (Sector1, Sector2, 
Industry) 
– Sector1 cross-references with IdxRlClsCode where IdxRlClsCode.Code = Sector1 
– Sector2 cross-references with IdxRlClsCode where IdxRlClsCode.Code = concatenation of (Sector1, Sector2)

text:
LSEG Quantitative Analytics  Database Schema for LSEG Climate 
 4 
CORPORATE 
1. Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the LSEG Climate tables in Quantitative Analytics. 
NOTE 
For information about the other Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other Database Schema documents posted on the 
Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

filename: QA Database Schema - LSEG Climate v1.1 (2025-07-08).pdf
text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
Note: Indexes are not applicable for Snowflake. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use LSEG Climate data through LSEG. 
Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in 
these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL 
Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with CLM* are the LSEG Climate 
data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

production.

saleable and 'Not Specified' indicates no production details.

filename: QA Database Schema - LSEG Climate v1.1 (2025-07-08).pdf
text:
Example: if the description of the item is Depreciation, Amortization 
and impairment expense which indicates a combination of items and 
does not have further breakdown of the same, then Combined Item 
Flag is ‘1’. Combined Item Flag is tagged to the financial concept 
code of the data item collected. 
Comments varchar(1000) Yes Comments provides information around the source document used 
and the exact page where the information is collected from.

helps clients to know from where the data is picked from the source 
document. 
ConvTypeName varchar(100) Yes Conversion Type Name contains information whether the 
conversion type is reported in the source document (Disclosed) or

in the company reports and the factor has been estimated.

item collected and indicates if the item is derived by the system and 
the reason for derivation. 
Derivation System Type Code is a two-letter code indicating the 
following reasons for derivation: 
– BI - Balancing Item, implies the system derived balance value in 
case of incomplete Parent-Child Relationship or breakdown or 
rounding off difference. 
– MP - Missing Period, implies that the derived value is a result of 
missing period calculation. 
– MR - Missing As Reported, implies that the derived values is a 
result of missing as-reported calculation 
– XB- XBRL - implies data from automation. 
– NA - Not Applicable. 
DerFlg char(1) Yes Derived Flag is associated with the financial data item collected and 
reflects ‘1’ if the item is derived by the system.

balancing item derived due to incomplete Parent-Child Relationship 
or breakdown or rounding off difference or value derived because of 
missing as-reported calculation.

the information is collected from the final document. 
Companies file both press and final reports for a financial period and 
Final Flag helps to identify if the value is collected from press or 
final. 
Final Flag reflects ‘0’ if the information is collected from a 
preliminary/press report. When the Final Flag value is ‘1’, it indicates 
that the value is from a final report.

document used to collect financial data for a particular period end.  
Data is collected from multiple source documents such as press, 
final, amendments for a particular period.

identifier which is a unique chronological numerical value for each 
company. 
Each document is assigned a Document Control Number (DCN) and 
records the filing date and time when the document is filed.

marked 0 if it is final document. Statement date is the period end 
date of the quarters or annual reports. FinanciallineitemSourceID-

FuelTypeName varchar(100) Yes Fuel type will contain the information about thermal coal, 
metallurgical coal, pulverized coal, anthracite coal, combination of 
metallurgical or pulverized coal, combination of thermal or 
pulverized coal, combination of thermal or metallurgical coal, 
combination of thermal or metallurgical or pulverized coal of the 
organization. 
The value 'Not Disclosed' indicates that the company is silent on the 
type of coal in the company reports and 'Not Applicable' is used 
when there are no mine details reported by the company. 
InstNum varchar(100) Yes Instance Number is associated with the financial data values derived 
or calculated by the system using the as-reported content. . 
Analytical data value may be derived either through summation, 
deduction, multiplication, or division using the as-reported value to 
provide meaningful ratios, and each value is assigned an Instance 
Number. Each analytical value is assigned with a unique identifier 
known as Instance Number. 
MineOwnCode varchar(50) Yes Mine Ownership Code contains information about the ownership of 
mine. 
Mines with ownership greater than or equal to 50% or Mines with 
ownership less than 50% are captured under this data element. 
ParentLineItem int Yes Parent Line Item ID is associated with the collection of financial data 
items and the capability to display the total value and its 
corresponding components as an indent. 
Generally, companies disclose the key totals on the face of the 
statements and its components or breakdowns in the footnotes. The 
total value is the parent line, and the components are child line 
items. 
Parent Line Item ID is a numerical value assigned to each 
component to which it is the parent line in the Parent-Child 
Relationship (PCR) to avoid double accounting.

1 Introduction

This document provides schema information about the LSEG ESG data  tables in Quantitative Analytics.

Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
Note: Indexes are not applicable for Snowflake. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use LSEG ESG data through LSEG. Note 
that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in these 
tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 
2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with ESG2* are the LSEG ESG data 
tables. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

billing, user management, and information.

MyAccount.

The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
This document provides descriptions of database schemas and definitions of database schema items. For more 
detailed explanations, refer to the LSEG Financials Glossary posted on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product 
page on MyAccount. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for LSEG Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use LSEG Financials data through 
LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data 
in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. 
Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In LSEG Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table 
name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with RKD* are the LSEG 
Financials data tables. 
ー Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. 
Vendor databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
ー Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
ー Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log 
schema description is available in the Database Schema for LSEG  Quantitative Analytics Core Tables 
document.) 
ー Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
ー Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the 
index fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
ー Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data 
types, and whether each field is nullable. Data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, 
an int in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake.

LSEG Financials Schema 
The LSEG Financials tables begin with the letters RKD.
The RKD schema is organized into these groups: 
LSEG Financials 
These tables begin with the prefix RKDFnd*. 
ー LSEG Financials Basic Company Information (page 9) 
ー LSEG Financials Company Industry Information and Reference Data (page 19) 
ー LSEG Financials Standardized Period and Filing Information (page 27) 
ー LSEG Financials Company-specific Period and Filing Information (page 36) 
ー LSEG Financials Calculated Ratios, Currencies, and Exchange Rates (page 46) 
ー LSEG Financials Business and Geographic Segment Data (page 50) 
ー LSEG Financials Officers and Directors Data (page 54) 
ー LSEG Financials Significant Developments Data (page 74) 
ー LSEG Financials General Information and Reference Information (page 77) 
ー LSEG Financials Major Customers Data (page 80) 
ー LSEG Financials Competitors Data (page 84) 
ー LSEG Financials Long Business Descriptions Data (page 86) 
ー LSEG Financials and Financials Point in Time Lookup Tables (page 88)
LSEG Financials Point in Time 
LSEG Financials Point in Time reference the Financials Point in Time Lookup Tables described on page 88. The 
Point in Time tables begin with the prefix RKDPIT2Fnd*. 
ー LSEG Financials Point in Time Company and Issue Details (page 90) 
ー LSEG Financials Point in Time Exchange Rates and Pricing Information (page 97) 
ー LSEG Financials Point in Time Standardized Periods and Filings (page 100) 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016.  
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index 
names and data types. Please note that references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of 
“–99999” or “–9999”; in these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) 
If the table contains a “0” value, the data was reported as having a “0” value.

DFlag: Additional Company Information 
DFlag is a field in the tables RKDFndCmpRef, RKDFndCmpRefIssue, and RKDPIT2FndCmpRef. 
Use DFlag to determine whether additional content exists for an item and to identify the type of information available. 
You can use this query to cross-reference DFlag with RKDFndCode. Change the query Select value (in this case 
238) so that it is the same as the item DFlag value. 
select 238 & code, desc_ 
from rkdfndcode 
where type_ = 59 
Output: The presence of a numeric code other than zero indicates that the corresponding content exists. When a zero 
is present, the corresponding content is not available for the item. Note that the DFlag value is derived by taking the 
sum of the available content codes from the output.

14. LSEG Financials and LSEG 
Financials PIT Lookup Tables 
The lookup tables contain integer and character code translations. These tables are shared between the LSEG 
Financials and LSEG Financials Point in Time (PIT) schemas. 
RKDFndCode
PK Type_
PK Code
 Desc_
RKDFndDesc
PK Type_
PK Code
 Desc_
Lookup table data is divided according to whether the referenced code is integer-based or character-based.  
Integer-based codes are translated in RKDFndCode, and character-based codes are translated in RKDFndDesc. 
In some cases, you may need to translate data between the tables. For example, for the table RKDFndCmpRef, 
currency codes are referenced as integers. In this case, you use RKDFndCode to translate the integer code into the 
three-character ISO currency code. You can then use RKDFndDesc to translate the ISO currency code into the 
common currency name. In both cases the referenced code maps to the same lookup table value, which for currency 
codes is Type_ = 58. 
To translate the currency code in one step, you can use this query: 
select a.type_, a.code, a.desc_, b.desc_ from rkdfndcode a 
left join rkdfnddesc b 
on a.type_ = b.type_ 
and a.desc_ = b.code 
where b.type_ = 58 
order by code
You can modify this code sample to work with other Type_ values as needed.

The SQL Views provide simplified calls that run complex SQL code and address key data nuances and mapping

Quantitative Analytics.  
The RQA Support Team is available to provide training on the library structure and how to use the SQL Views.

vw_RKDPitMapping 
Multiple securities under the same company mostly have the same set of fundamental data and RepNo. At the 
same time, it is possible for securities listed in different countries to follow different accounting standards. 
Therefore, the same company may be required to provide separate filings under different RepNo. 
RKD PIT tries to limit the number of RepNo with fundamental data under the same company. This view shows the 
best mapping practices when mapping QAID to RKDPIT.

The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use LSEG Indices data through LSEG. 
Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in 
these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL 
Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with IdxTR* are LSEG Indices data 
tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle.

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the MarketPsych Analytics data tables in LSEG Quantitative 
Analytics. 
NOTE 
For information about the other Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other Database Schema documents posted on the 
Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use MarketPsych Analytics data through 
LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the 
data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft 
SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, tables that begin with MPI* are MarketPsych Analytics  
data tables. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

billing, user management, and information.

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the MSCI data tables in Quantitative Analytics.

Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

filename: QA Database Schema - MSCI v1.0.5 (2023-05-05).pdf
text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use MSCI data through LSEG. Note that 
the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in these tables 
is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with MS2* are MSCI Version 2 data 
tables. All tables beginning with MS* are MSCI legacy data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

2. MSCI Version 2 Schema 
Design Notes 
Empty Tables 
The MSCI version 2 schema was designed to be flexible, enabling new data items to be included easily if/when 
they are provided by MSCI.  
In this design, the data is organized in tables by index or security and then by data type. For example, daily index 
data is contained in MSDIDXDLY in the legacy implementation. In the version 2 implementation, this data is 
contained in multiple tables by data type: MS2IdxDDly (date data), MS2IdxFDly (float data), MS2IdxIDly (integer 
data), and MS2IdxSDly (string varchar data).  
To maintain the symmetry of this design and enable the addition of future items with limited impact to clients, 
several tables were created that are not currently populated. We may populate these tables if/when additional 
data items are provided by MSCI. But, in the current design (as of January 2012), these tables are intentionally 
empty: 
– MS2IdxDDly 
– MS2SecDDly 
– MS2IdxIDly 
– MS2SecDivMth 
– MS2IdxSDly 
– MS2SecIDly 
– MS2SecD 
– MS2SecSDly 
– MS2SecDACE 
Table Name Format 
The names of the MSCI version 2 data tables reflect the type of data items they contain. The table name format is 
MS2[Idx|Sec][Datatype][Frq][ACE] where: 
– [Idx|Sec] indicates whether the data is index-level or security-level. 
– [Datatype] indicates the type of data: I = integer data, S = varchar data, D = date data, F = float data, and 
SMax = very large varchar data. 
– [Frq] indicates whether the data is daily or monthly. "Mth" indicates monthly data. Both "Dly" and no [Frq] suffix 
indicate daily data. The difference is that items in the "*Dly" tables are updated daily (usually pricing related). 
Items in a table with no [Frq] value change infrequently; we get updates for these every day, but generally the 
value is the same every day.  
– The tables with a "Dly" or "Mth" suffix have a single Date_ field. The tables without either suffix have a 
StartDate/EndDate pair. Tables with the "Mth" suffix are included for clients with a monthly or daily license. 
Tables with no suffix or with the "Dly" suffix are only given to clients with a daily license. 
– [ACE] indicates whether the data is ACE data. If a table name ends with "ACE", it contains ACE data. If not, 
the table does not contain ACE data.

MS2IdxConstDly: Daily MSCI Index Constituents 
This table contains daily MSCI index constituents data.

Update Cycle: Daily 
Adjusted: N/A 
Indexes Index Fields 
pkey_MS2IdxConstDly (Clustered) MSCICode, SecID, StartDate
Field  Type  Nullable Description 
MSCICode int N MSCICode is the MSCI index identifier. It is the primary link across all 
MS2Idx* tables. MSCICode is defined in MS2IdxInfo. 
SecID int N SecID is the security ID.
StartDate datetime N If you are licensed for MSCI Deep History content: 
– StartDate is the date the security became part of the index.
If you are not licensed for MSCI Deep History content: 
– If StartDate is more recent than 13 months ago from today (the beginning 
of the daily data rolling window), StartDate is the date the security 
became part of the index. In this scenario, the security joined the index 
within the current 13-month rolling window.  
– A StartDate that is older than 13 months ago from today indicates the 
security joined the index prior to the beginning of the 13-month rolling 
window. In this scenario, the value of StartDate does not represent the 
actual date the security joined the index. To receive the actual date the 
security joined the index, you must be licensed for MSCI Deep History 
content. 
EndDate datetime Y When applicable, EndDate is the date the security was removed from the 
index. 
TotIncFactor float Y TotIncFactor is the total inclusion factor. This is a derived field created by 
LSEG Quantitative Analytics. 
NextTotIncFactor float Y NextTotIncFactor is the next day total inclusion factor. 
LicFlag int Y LicFlag is a bit value that represents the license for this table.

This table is populated going forward from 2011.

text:
DivDesc tinyint Y DivDesc is the MSCI dividend description: 
– 0 = Annual 
– 1 = Final 
– 2 = Interim 
– 3 = Quarterly 
– 4 = Extra 
– 5 = Monthly 
– 6 = Regular 
– 7 = Commemorative 
This field cross-references with MS2Code.Code where Type_ = 5. 
XDDate datetime Y XDDate is the dividend ex-date. 
CorrectionFlag tinyint Y CorrectionFlag indicates that the dividend amount is a correction of an 
already reinvested dividend. The difference between the correct and 
incorrect amount will show in the gross dividend amount, net dividend 
amount international, and net dividend amount domestic. 
ReinvDate datetime Y ReinvDate is the date as of which the dividend is reinvested in the index. 
Div float Y Div is the declared dividend amount. 
AdjGRSDiv float Y AdjGRSDiv is the gross dividend amount of withholding taxes to be 
reinvested in MSCI Daily Gross Total Return Indices. 
AdjNETDiv float Y AdjNETDiv is the net dividend amount of withholding taxes to be 
reinvested in MSCI Daily Net Total Return Indices for MSCI international 
indices. 
ISOCurrCode char(3) Y ISOCurrCode is the dividend ISO currency symbol. This field cross-
references with MS2Desc.Code where Type_ = 2. 
DivSubUnit float Y DivSubUnit is the dividend sub-unit. It indicates whether the dividend 
amount is expressed for one share (1.000) or in lot (0.001); some 
securities in Brazil are provided in lot of 1000.  
DivAdjFactor float Y DivAdjFactor is the dividend adjustment factor. It reflects the impact of 
corporate events on the declared dividend amount. 
DTRNumShares float Y DTRNumShares is the number of shares used in the calculation of the 
MSCI DTR Indices, as of the dividend ex date, minus one. 
LicFlag int Y LicFlag is a bit value that represents the license for this table.

 30

MS2SecInfo: MSCI Security Information 
This table contains MSCI security information.
Update Cycle: Daily 
NOTE 
Unless you are licensed for MSCI Deep History, the data in this table is purged on a 13-month rolling basis.
Adjusted: N/A 
Indexes Index Fields 
pkey_MS2SecInfo (Clustered) SecID
Field  Type  Nullable Description 
SecID int N SecID is the security ID. 
TsCode int Y TsCode is the MSCI time series code and unique security identifier. 
IssCode int Y IssCode is the MSCI issuer code. Not all issuers have an IssCode. 
SecCode int Y SecCode is the MSCI security code. 
Name_ varchar(40) Y Name_ is the name of the security. 
ISOCtryCode char(2) Y ISOCtryCode is the ISO country code. It is a two-digit alphabetic code 
for country classification. MS2SecInfo.ISOCtryCode joins with 
MS2Desc.Code where Type_ = 1. 
NextISOCtryCode char(2) Y NextISOCtryCode Is the next day ISO country code. 
MIC char(4) Y MIC is the market identifier code. It specifies a universal method of 
identifying exchanges and trading platforms and regulated or non-
regulated markets as sources of prices and related information in order 
to facilitate automated processing. 
NextMIC char(4) Y NextMIC is the next day market identifier code. 
BloomTkr varchar(25) Y BloomTkr is the Bloomberg ticker. 
NextBloomTkr varchar(25) Y NextBloomTkr is the next day Bloomberg ticker. 
ShareClassCode tinyint Y ShareClassCode is the share class code. It provides information on the 
main category of the security (for example, COMMON, PREFERRED, 
and UNIT). MS2SecInfo.ShareClassCode joins with MS2Code.Code 
where Type_ = 8. 
ShareTypeCode tinyint Y ShareTypeCode is the share type code. It provides information on the 
sub-category of the security (for example, A, B, and H). 
MS2SecInfo.ShareTypeCode joins with MS2Code.Code where Type_ = 
9. 
AltListingCode tinyint Y AltListingCode is the alternate listing code. It provides information on 
the listing of the security (for example, ADR and GDR). 
MS2SecInfo.AltListingCode joins with MS2Code.Code where Type_ = 
10. 
BarraID char(8) Y BarraID is the Barra security identifier. 
EndDate datetime Y EndDate is the date the period ends. 
ModDate datetime Y ModDate is the date the security information was last modified. 
LicFlag int Y LicFlag is a bit value that represents the license for this table.

text:
Relationship Between MS2Item and MS2ItemMap 
Use MS2ItemMap to determine the table in which a particular data item from MS2Item is stored. Each MSCI 
version 2 data item is stored in one or more tables. The location of a specific data item depends on whether it is 
index- or security-level, the data type, how often it is updated (daily or monthly), and whether it is Advanced 
Corporate Event (ACE) data.  
The names of the MSCI version 2 data tables reflect the the type of data items they contain. The table name 
format is MS2[Idx|Sec][Datatype][Frq][ACE]. For details about this table name format, see Table Name Format 
on page 6. The following query returns the full mapping of the MSCI version 2 data items and corresponding data 
tables. 
select i.Item, i.Mnemonic, i.Desc_, i.AdjCode, i.ParentItem,  
      i.DataTypeCode, i.DecimalNum, i.BoxFlg, i.DSFlg,  
      i.BasicFlg, i.EnhFlg, i.LegacyMnem,  
      m.SecFlg, m.IdxFlg, m.FrqFlg, m.DlyFlg, m.MthFlg, m.ACEFlg, m.TableName 
from MS2Item i 
join MS2ItemMap m 
on m.DataTypeCode = i.DataTypeCode 
and ((m.SecFlg = i.SecFlg) or (m.IdxFlg = i.IdxFlg)) -- AN ITEM MAY BE SECURITY LEVEL, 
INDEX LEVEL OR BOTH 
and ((m.MthFlg = i.MthFlg)  
or (m.DlyFlg = i.DlyFlg and m.FrqFlg = i.FrqFlg)) -- AN ITEM MAY BE MONTHLY OR 
DAILY.  IF DAILY, THE TABLE DETERMINED BY  FREQUENCY FLAGS 
--and m.ACEFlg = 1 -- FOR ADVANCE CORPORATE ACTION (ACE) ITEMS 
--and m.SecFlg = 1 -- INCLUDE FOR SECURITY LEVEL ITEMS 
--and m.IdxFlg = 1 -- INCLUDE FOR INDEX LEVEL ITEMS 
--and m.MthFlg = 1 -- INCLUDE FOR MONTHLY ITEMS 
--and m.DlyFlg = 1 -- INCLUDE FOR DAILY ITEMS
