The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Northfield Risk Factors data through 
LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the 
data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft 
SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with NF* are Northfield Risk 
Factors data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle.

Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Ownership and Global Insider data 
through LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access 
to the data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of 
Microsoft SQL Server 2016.

In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with OWN* are Ownership and 
Global Insider data tables.

This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”,

Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

OwnSecCumAdjFact*: Cumulative Adjustment Factors 
Use factor tables to make split-related adjustments to the data in the OwnSecData and OwnHoldDet tables.
There are three cumulative adjustment factor tables: 
– OwnSecCumAdjFactD (Daily) 
– OwnSecCumAdjFactQ (Quarterly) 
– OwnSecCumAdjFactW (Weekly) 
The factor table you should use is indicated by FeedType. For example, if OwnHoldDet.FeedType = D, this 
indicates the record references the cumulative factor from the Daily factor table, OwnSecCumAdjFactD.
Update Cycle:  OwnSecCumAdjFactD: Daily 
OwnSecCumAdjFactQ: Quarterly 
OwnSecCumAdjFactW: Weekly 
Adjusted: N/A 
Indexes Index Fields 
pkey_OwnSecCumAdjFact[D, Q, or W] (Clustered) SecurityCode
Field Type Nullable Description 
SecurityCode int N SecurityCode is the unique identifier for a security. It is defined by OwnSecInfo. This 
field links to all Security data tables. 
CumFact float Y CumFact is the cumulative factor to apply to the security based on all historical splits 
and corporate actions. Because the factor value takes into account the differences in 
the frequency of the feeds, this figure may be different depending on whether you 
are viewing the daily, weekly, or quarterly data.
NOTE 
See OwnSecData on page 16 and OwnHoldDet on page 21. 
OwnSecCumAdjRatio*: Corporate Actions Cumulative History 
These tables capture the cumulative history of the corporate actions for one or more securities described in 
OwnSecData and OwnHoldDet.
There are three corporate actions cumulative history tables: 
– OwnSecCumAdjRatioD (Daily) 
– OwnSecCumAdjRatioQ (Quarterly) 
– OwnSecCumAdjRatioW (Weekly) 
The ratio table you should refer to is indicated by FeedType. For example, if OwnSecData.FeedType = D, this 
indicates that the record was last updated by the daily feed and, as a result, you should refer to the Daily ratio 
table (OwnSecCumAdjRationD) for the latest cumulative ratio value. 
Ratio tables are provided for your convenience and are intended only for your reference. They are used primarily 
to compute the factor values in the factor tables.

Examples 
This section includes sample queries demonstrating how to return all securities by the same issuer, and how to 
use an owner ID to return the holdings of the owner on a given date. 
These examples reference the TRQA core master tables. For more information about the master tables, see the 
Database Schema for LSEG Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document, available on the LSEG Quantitative 
Analytics product page on MyAccount. 
Example 1: Securities by Issuer 
This query takes a given domestic ID and returns all securities linked to the given ID by the same Issuer.
DECLARE @ID VARCHAR(20) 
SET   @ID = 'IBM' -- IBM
SELECT  T.VENNAME 
  , S2.ID 
  , O.ISSUERNAME 
  , I2.SECNAME 
  , I2.CUSIP 
  , D.DESC_ AS SECURITY_CLASS
FROM   QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMSTRX S
JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMAPX M 
   ON  M.SECCODE = S.SECCODE 
   AND  M.VENTYPE = 21 
   AND  M.RANK = 1
JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNSECINFO I 
   ON  I.SECURITYCODE = M.VENCODE 
 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNSECISSUER O 
   ON  O.ISSUERCODE = I.ISSUERCODE 
 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.OWNSECINFO I2 
   ON  I2.ISSUERCODE = I.ISSUERCODE 
 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECMAPX M2 
   ON  M2.VENCODE = I2.SECURITYCODE 
   AND  M2.VENTYPE = 21  
 JOIN QAI_MASTER.DBO.SECVENTYPE T 
   ON  M.VENTYPE = T.VENTYPE

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the Ownership Version 2 tables in LSEG Quantitative

The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Ownership Version 2 data through 
LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the 
data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft 
SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with OWN2* are the Ownership 
Version 2 data tables. 
Mapping Information 
Use Ownership data to obtain information about large-scale holders of specific securities. 
The Quantitative Analytics schema for Ownership Version 2 is organized into several categories: 
– Holdings data 
– Unconsolidated 
– Consolidated 
– Investor data 
– Profile 
– Contacts 
– Transaction (Insider date)

Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

The SQL Views provide simplified calls that run complex SQL code and address key data nuances and mapping 
requests in the Quantitative Analytics database, making it much easier to access data through LSEG Quantitative

Customers are able to see the underlying SQL code and modify/customize it as required, as well as being able to

Our Support Team is available to provide training on the library structure and how to use the SQL Views. Please 
contact Support if you would like the SQL views added to your server.

This view provides the mapping for OwnershipIDs using RDC.  
Index Fields

Field Type Nullable Description 
InstrID int no InstrID is the Permanent Identifier of the instrument.  
InstrStatusCode char yes For non-debt issues, if an issue asset/instrument has at least 
one quote that is active (AssetState = 'AC'), then AssetState is 
Active 'AC'. If all quote assets are deactivated (AssetState = 
'DC'), then AssetState is Deactivated 'DC'. AssetState is 
derived for all asset types except debt issues that are 
maintained by the DBS forward feed.  
AssetState is 'NA' (Not Applicable) when no quote asset is 
found against the issue/instrument. In particular, new issues 
get 'NA' status as soon as they are created and until a quote is 
assigned to them. NA also applies to instruments not properly 
classified. States other than AC, DC, and NA are only set for 
fixed income issues.

fields). All changes made to these fields will trigger a matching 
change to be made to IssueISOCurrCode.

– MIFID-E: Mifid eligible security  
– MIFID-L: Mifid top liquidity security

was first admitted to trading on a regulated market.

used. This is very US-specific where market cap for the issue 
must be calculated on a consolidated quote that is not a RIC 
you can trade. Therefore, PrimTrdQuotePI exists to denote the 
main "primary" quote of a multi-listed share line in the US that 
can be traded.

1. Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the Reference Data Convergence (RDC) data tables in 
LSEG Quantitative Analytics. 
Note: For information about the other LSEG Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other 
Database Schema documents posted on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page 
on MyAccount.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– hVendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for LSEG Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for LSEG Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use TRBC data through LSEG. 
Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in 
these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. 
Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In LSEG Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table 
name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with RDC* are Reference 
Data Convergence (RDC) data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016.  
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in 
index names and data types. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle.

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the S&P GICS data tables in Quantitative Analytics. 
NOTE 
For information about the other Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other Database Schema documents posted on the 
Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

filename: QA Database Schema - S-P GICS v1.0.4 (2022-05-02).pdf
text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use S&P GICS data through LSEG. Note 
that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in these 
tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 
2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with SPG* are S&P GICS data 
tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle.

Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

MyAccount is the LSEG portal that provides a single access point for timesaving support services, along with

The Quantitative Analytics Service Description is available on the Quantitative Analytics product page at

Subscribe to Support Channels 
You are encouraged to subscribe to the following support channels to keep informed of changes to products and 
data, and to be notified of any service issues or change. Please see the Alerts and Notifications section in the 
Quantitative Analytics Service Description available on the Quantitative Analytics product page at MyAccount for 
detailed instructions. 
– Change Notifications 
– Product Change Notifications (PCNs) detail new, enhanced, or changed functionality, which may require 
your action, in products that you use. 
– Data Notifications (DNs) alert you to upcoming changes to real-time and historical data across all asset 
classes that are relevant to you. 
– RIC Change Events inform you of planned changes to RICs. RIC is the market level identifier key unique to 
LSEG used to identify securities. 
– Service Alerts 
Alert you about planned maintenance and unplanned service issues affecting your products and services, and 
be notified via SMS or email. 
Documentation

Online

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Short Interest data through LSEG. 
Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in 
these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL 
Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with ShortInt2* are Short Interest 
tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the StarMine Analytics data tables in Refinitiv 
Quantitative Analytics deployed and in the cloud.

Database Schema documents posted on the Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics product page on

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
• Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. 
Vendor databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
• Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of 
the table contents. 
• Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log 
schema description is available in the Database Schema for Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics Core 
Tables document.) 
• Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is 
not applicable (N/A). 
• Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the 
index fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
• Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, 
data types, and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents 
available. For example, an int in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use StarMine Analytics 
data through Refinitiv. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several 
licenses; your access to the data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. 
Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of 
the table name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight 
differences in index names and data types. Please note that references to Pervasive and Actian are 
synonymous.

If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved 
words are appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” 
become “Number_”, “Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. A table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in these 
cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) 
If the table contains a “0” value, the data was reported as having a “0” value.

product page at MyRefinitiv.

products and data, and to be notified of any service issues or change. Please see the Alerts and 
Notifications section in the Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics Service Description available on the Refinitiv 
Quantitative Analytics product page at MyRefinitiv for detailed instructions. 
• Change Notifications 
• Product Change Notifications (PCNs) detail new, enhanced, or changed functionality, which 
may require your action, in products that you use. 
• Content Notifications (DNs) alert you to upcoming changes to real-time and historical data 
across all asset classes that are relevant to you. 
• RIC Change Events inform you of planned changes to Refinitiv Identification Codes.  
• Service Alerts 
Alert you about planned maintenance and unplanned service issues affecting your products and 
services and be notified via SMS or email. 
Documentation 
You can access product documentation on the Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics product page at 
MyRefinitiv.

Online 
Access Get Support either via the blue Get Support button at the top right of each page or by selecting 
Get Support located under Help and Support on the left navigation pane at MyRefinitiv.

Database Schema for Starmine Data
1. Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the StarMine data tables in LSEG Quantitative Analytics. 
NOTE. For information about the other LSEG Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other Database Schema documents 
posted on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options.

filename: QA Database Schema - StarMine v1.1.4 (2024-01-22).pdf
text:
Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the table 
contents. 
Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific information 
about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema description is 
available in the Database Schema for LSEG Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int in 
SQL Server is a number  
in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for LSEG Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use StarMine data through LSEG. 
Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in 
these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. 
Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In LSEG Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table 
name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with SM2* are StarMine 
tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in 
index names and data types. Please note that references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. A table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in these cases, 
there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) 
If the table contains a “0” value, the data was reported as having a “0” value.

 12 
3. StarMine Regional Data 
Model Tables 
StarMine data is organized first by data model, and then by region. Availability of data depends on your  
data license. 
Data Models 
The StarMine data models are: 
– ARM (Analyst Revision Models): table names begin with Sm2DArm* 
– CRM (Credit Risk Models): table names begin with Sm2DCRM* 
– EQ (Earnings Quality): table names begin with Sm2DEq* 
– IV (Intrinsic Value): table names begin with Sm2DIv* 
– Smart Holdings: table names begin with Sm2DSH* 
– Val-Mo (Value Momentum) and Price-Mo (Price Momentum): table names begin with Sm2DVMo*.  
The Val-Mo model combines the StarMine ARM and IV Regional Models with the Price-Mo factor. 
NOTE. To access Daily Val-Mo Model data you must be licensed for StarMine ARM and IV daily regional Models. The Daily Val-
Mo model license includes Price-Mo Daily data; however, Price- Mo may also be licensed separately.
Regional Data Categories 
StarMine regional data is divided into these categories: 
– Americas: table names end in *AM 
– Asia Pacific: table names end in *AP 
– Europe, Middle East, and Africa: table names end in *EA 
Regional tables are organized identically and differ only by name and content. For this reason, regional tables 
share common descriptions. For example, the description for Sm2DArm* applies to the regional ARM tables 
Sm2DArmAM, Sm2DArmAP, and Sm2DArmEA. 
Regional Daily Data Adjustments 
Regional data is updated daily, and the data is unadjusted. StarMine Daily data is provided "as was," so it is not 
adjusted for any corporate actions. Any historical data items which require split adjustments are applied by 
StarMine and are refreshed with each monthly update.

5. SQL Views 
The SQL Views1 provide simplified calls that run complex SQL code and address key data nuances and mapping 
requests in the LSEG Quantitative Analytics database, making it much easier to access data through LSEG 
Quantitative Analytics. 
Customers are able to see the underlying SQL code and modify/customize it as required, as well as being able to 
save the modified code as their proprietary code. 
The LSEG Support Team is available to provide training on the library structure and how to use the SQL Views. 
Please contact support if you would like the SQL views added to your server. 
The SQL Views were introduced in LSEG Quantitative Analytics Release 6.35 in May 2017. 
vw_SM2MappingDaily 
This view can be used to map to the Daily StarMine Model data (ventype 23).

Field Type Nullable Description

select aa.SecCode, bb.Exchange, bb.Rank, cc.CmpName, cc.Ticker, cc.SecId

where aa.ItemDesc like '%margin%' -- Find all the “margin” items.

refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, tables that begin with MMS* are StarMine MarketPsych

Database Schema for Symbology  
 3 
1. Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the Symbology data tables in LSEG Quantitative Analytics. 
Note: For information about the other LSEG Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other Database Schema 
documents posted on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

filename: QA Database Schema - Symbology_v1.1.9.pdf
text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the table 
contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific information 
about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema description is 
available in the Database Schema for LSEG Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int in 
SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for LSEG Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Symbology data through LSEG. 
Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in these 
tables is dependent on the licenses you have. 
Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In LSEG Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table 
name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables beginning with Perm* are Symbology data 
tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index 
names and data types. Please note that references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. A table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in these cases, there 
is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) 
If the table contains a “0” value, the data was reported as having a “0” value.

Service and Support 
MyAccount is the LSEG portal that provides a single access point for timesaving support services, along with billing, 
user management, and information.  
Statement of Service 
The LSEG Quantitative Analytics Service Description is available on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page at 
MyAccount. 
Subscribe to Support Channels 
You are encouraged to subscribe to the following support channels to keep informed of changes to products and 
data, and to be notified of any service issues or change. Please see the Alerts and Notifications section in the LSEG 
Quantitative Analytics Service Description available on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page at MyAccount 
for detailed instructions. 
– Change Notifications 
– Product Change Notifications (PCNs) detail new, enhanced, or changed functionality, which may require your 
action, in products that you use. 
– Content Notifications (DNs) alert you to upcoming changes to real-time and historical data across all asset 
classes that are relevant to you. 
– RIC Change Events inform you of planned changes to LSEG Identification Codes.  
– Service Alerts 
Alert you about planned maintenance and unplanned service issues affecting your products and services, and be 
notified via SMS or email. 
Documentation 
You can access product documentation on the LSEG Quantitative Analytics product page at MyAccount. 
Get Support 
For support using LSEG Quantitative Analytics, please use one of the following methods: 
Online 
Access Get Support either via the blue Get Support button at the top right of each page or by selecting Get Support 
located under Help and Support on the left navigation pane at MyAccount.  
From the Get Support page, choose Get Product and Content Support and then select the appropriate category from 
the next page.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Toyo Keizai data through LSEG. 
Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in 
these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL 
Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with TK2* are Toyo Keizai Version 
2 data tables. 
Toyo Keizai Version 2 and Legacy Toyo Keizai 
Due to changes in the Toyo Keizai datafeed, Quantitative Analytics release 5.84 contains Toyo Keizai version 2. 
The Toyo Keizai Version 2 schema contains the TREND3EPOT datafeed and supercedes the Toyo Keizai 
schema that existed prior to release 5.84. The pre-5.84 schema is now considered "legacy." Tables in the legacy 
Toyo Keizai schema begin with the letters TK (rather than TK2). 
The legacy tables will be discontinued in the future on a date yet to be determined. In the meantime, they remain 
supported by LSEG Quantitative Analytics. It is recommended that you upgrade to the LSEG Financials schema 
on LSEG Quantitative Analytics deployed version 5.84 (minimum) to ensure continued support of your data.

Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the The Reference Business Classification (TRBC) data 
tables in Quantitative Analytics. 
NOTE 
For information about the other Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other Database Schema documents posted on the 
Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the table 
contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific information 
about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema description is 
available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use The Reference Business 
Classification (TRBC) data through LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by 
several licenses; your access to the data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should 
have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with RDCTRBC* are The Reference 
Business Classification (TRBC) data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle.

Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

user management, and information.

MyAccount.

data, and to be notified of any service issues or change. Please see the Alerts and Notifications section in the 
Quantitative Analytics Service Description available on the Quantitative Analytics product page at MyAccount for 
detailed instructions. 
– Change Notifications

your action, in products that you use. 
– Data Notifications (DNs) alert you to upcoming changes to real-time and historical data across all asset 
classes that are relevant to you. 
– RIC Change Events inform you of planned changes to RICs. RIC is the market level identifier key unique to 
LSEG used to identify securities. 
– Service Alerts 
Alert you about planned maintenance and unplanned service issues affecting your products and services, and be 
notified via SMS or email.

Online

Support located under Help and Support on the left navigation pane at MyAccount.  
From the Get Support page, choose Get Product and Content Support and then select the appropriate category

RDCTRBCMap: TRBC Mapping Information 
TRBC uses a 5-level hierarchical system with 10 economic sectors, 28 business sectors, 54 industry groups, 136 
industries, and 837 Activity codes. This table captures the association between all levels. 
An Activity is a new, more granular industry level within TRBC. For the first time users will have an investment 
focused alternative to NAICS and SIC codes.

3. SQL Views  
The SQL Views provide simplified calls that run complex SQL code and address key data nuances and mapping 
requests in the LSEG Quantitative Analytics database, making it much easier to access data through LSEG 
Quantitative Analytics.  
Customers are able to see the underlying SQL code and modify/customize it as required, as well as being able to 
save the modified code as their proprietary code.  
The LSEG Support Team is available to provide training on the library structure and how to use the SQL Views. 
Please contact Support if you would like the SQL views added to your server.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use US Insider data through LSEG. Note 
that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access to the data in these 
tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 
2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with INS* are US Insider data 
tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of “–99999” or “–9999”; in 
these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) If the table contains a “0” value, the data was 
reported as having a “0” value.

The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. Vendor 
databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment is not 
applicable (N/A). 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Worldscope Point in Time data 
through LSEG. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; your access 
to the data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. Readers should have basic knowledge of 
Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table name 
refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with WSPIT* are Worldscope Point 
in Time data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016. If you are accessing the data directly through the 
Pervasive database, you may encounter slight differences in index names and data types. Please note that 
references to Pervasive and Actian are synonymous. 
If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved words are 
appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” become “Number_”, 
“Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle.

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides schema information about the Worldscope data tables in Refinitiv Quantitative 
Analytics. 
Note: For information about the other Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other 
Database Schema documents posted on the Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics product page on 
MyRefinitiv.

text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
• Vendor Database or License Name – This element provides the vendor database or license name. 
Vendor databases generally correspond to vendor licensing options. 
• Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description 
of the table contents. 
• Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log 
schema description is available in the Database Schema for Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics Core 
Tables document.) 
• Adjusted – This element indicates whether the data is stored adjusted, unadjusted, or if adjustment 
is not applicable (N/A). 
• Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and 
the index fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
• Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, 
data types, and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents 
available. For example, an int in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics clients licensed to use Worldscope data 
through Refinitiv. Note that the tables described in this document may be covered by several licenses; 
your access to the data in these tables is dependent on the licenses you have. 
Readers should have basic knowledge of Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
In Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics, database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of 
the table name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. For example, all tables that begin with WS* 
are Wordscope data tables. 
Pervasive and Oracle 
This document is specific to Microsoft SQL Server 2016.  
If you are accessing the data directly through the Pervasive database, you may encounter slight 
differences in index names and data types.

If you are accessing the data through Oracle, note that field names that correspond to Oracle reserved 
words are appended with an underscore. For example, field names “Number”, “Synonym”, and “UID” 
become “Number_”, “Synonym_”, and “UID_” in Oracle. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. Occasionally, a table may contain a value of 
“–99999” or “–9999”; in these cases, there is no recorded data for that period. (It is null.) 
If the table contains a “0” value, the data was reported as having a “0” value. 
Service and Support 
MyRefinitiv is the Refinitiv portal that provides a single access point for timesaving support services, along 
with billing, user management, and information.  
Statement of Service 
The Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics Service Description is available on the Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics 
product page at MyRefinitiv. 
Subscribe to Support Channels 
You are encouraged to subscribe to the following support channels to keep informed of changes to 
products and data, and to be notified of any service issues or change. Please see the Alerts and 
Notifications section in the Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics Service Description available on the Refinitiv 
Quantitative Analytics product page at MyRefinitiv for detailed instructions. 
• Change Notifications 
• Product Change Notifications (PCNs) detail new, enhanced, or changed functionality, which 
may require your action, in products that you use. 
• Content Notifications (DNs) alert you to upcoming changes to real-time and historical data 
across all asset classes that are relevant to you. 
• RIC Change Events inform you of planned changes to Refinitiv Identification Codes.  
• Service Alerts 
Alert you about planned maintenance and unplanned service issues affecting your products and 
services, and be notified via SMS or email. 
Documentation 
You can access product documentation on the Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics product page at 
MyRefinitiv. 
Get Support 
For support using Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics, please use one of the following methods: 
Online 
Access Get Support either via the blue  Get Support  button at the top right of each page or by selecting 
Get Support located under Help and Support on the left navigation pane at MyRefinitiv.

4 SQL Views 
A library of sophisticated SQL Views, developed by the Refinitiv Support Team, are available to 
customers. The SQL Views provide simplified calls that run complex SQL code and address key data 
nuances and mapping requests in the Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics database, making it much easier to 
access data through Refinitiv Quantitative Analytics. 
Customers are able to see the underlying SQL code and modify/customize it as required. Customers are 
also able to save the modified code as their proprietary code. 
The Support Team provides training to users on the library structure and how to use the SQL Views. 
Note: Contact Support via one of the methods under Get Support for access to the SQL Views.  
vw_WSItemUnits 
This view shows whether a Worldscope item measure shares, people, currency or currency per share. 
Index Fields 
code (part of compound index) 
item 
itemName
Field Type Nullable Description 
code Int N code is the primary link across all Worldscope (Ws*) tables. 
item Int N item cross-references with all Ws*DATA tables where 
item = Ws*data.Item. 
itemName varchar(55) Y itemName is the name of the data item. 
itemUnits varchar(9) Y itemUnits describes the units this item is stored in and can be: 
• ‘Shares’ 
• ‘Persons’ 
• currency eg ‘USD’ 
• currency per share eg ‘CHF/share’ 
Note: This is the Worldscope currency and not the reported 
currency
Example Use Case:
Select 
itemName, itemUnits 
from vw_WSItemUnits 
where item = 1001 -- net sales or revenues 
and code = 51904 -- Thomson Reuters

1 Introduction 
In This Document 
This document provides an overview of the schemas, tables, and fields available in LSEG Quantitative Analytics 
database schema documents. 
NOTE 
For information about the other Quantitative Analytics tables, refer to the other Database Schema documents posted on the 
Quantitative Analytics product page on MyAccount.

filename: Quantitative Analytics Schema Catalog v1.0.pdf
text:
The documentation for each table includes these main elements: 
– Table Name: Table Title – This element provides the table name and title, followed by a description of the 
table contents. 
– Update Cycle – This element indicates the frequency of updates from the data vendor. (For specific 
information about when this update is posted for your use, refer to your update logs. The update log schema 
description is available in the Database Schema for Quantitative Analytics Core Tables document.) 
– Indexes, Index Fields – This element lists the table’s index(es) (for example, pkey_CSGCAD) and the index 
fields. The primary index contains a “pkey_” or “PK_” prefix. Clustered indexes are noted. 
– Field, Type, Nullable, Definition – This element describes the table’s fields, including field names, data types, 
and whether each field is nullable. The data types in Snowflake have equivalents available. For example, an int 
in SQL Server is a number in Snowflake. 
Intended Readership 
This document is intended for LSEG Quantitative Analytics clients. Readers should have basic knowledge of 
Microsoft SQL Server 2016. 
Table Name Conventions 
LSEG Quantitative Analytics database tables are grouped by name. Generally, the first few letters of the table 
name refer to the data vendor or licensing group. 
Zero Values and Nulls 
Null values are usually recorded as “NULL”. If the table contains a “0” value, the data was reported as having a 
“0” value. 
Service and Support 
MyAccount is the LSEG portal that provides a single access point for timesaving support services, along with 
billing, user management, and information.  
Statement of Service 
The Quantitative Analytics Service Description is available on the Quantitative Analytics product page at 
MyAccount. 
Subscribe to Support Channels 
You are encouraged to subscribe to the following support channels to keep informed of changes to products and 
data, and to be notified of any service issues or change. Please see the Alerts and Notifications section in the 
Quantitative Analytics Service Description available on the Quantitative Analytics product page at MyAccount for 
detailed instructions.

– Change Notifications 
– Product Change Notifications (PCNs) detail new, enhanced, or changed functionality, which may require 
your action, in products that you use. 
– Data Notifications (DNs) alert you to upcoming changes to real-time and historical data across all asset 
classes that are relevant to you. 
– RIC Change Events inform you of planned changes to RICs. RIC is the market level identifier key unique to 
LSEG used to identify securities. 
– Service Alerts 
Alert you about planned maintenance and unplanned service issues affecting your products and services, and 
be notified via SMS or email. 
Documentation 
You can access product documentation on the Quantitative Analytics product page at MyAccount. 
Get Support 
For support using Quantitative Analytics, please use one of the following methods: 
Online 
Access Get Support either via the blue Get Support button at the top right of each page or by selecting Get 
Support located under Help and Support on the left navigation pane at MyAccount.  
From the Get Support page, choose Get Product and Content Support and then select the appropriate category 
from the next page.
Complete the request making sure to include the following: 
– Under Product, select Quantitative Analytics from the dropdown list. 
– In the How can we help you? text box, include the following information: 
– Content set name (i.e. Worldscope) 
– Date applicable to a content inquiry 
– Table names and relevant fields 
– Security code (i.e. QA-ID, PermID, Sedol, InfoCode, etc.) 
– Script used to generate the output 
– Any other supporting detail

Feedback 
We invite your comments, corrections, and suggestions about this document: access the Feedback option under 
Get Support at MyAccount. Your feedback helps us continue to improve our user assistance. 
Your Personal Information 
LSEG is committed to the responsible handling and protection of personal information. We invite you to review 
our Privacy Statement, which describes how we collect, use, disclose, transfer, and store personal information 
when needed to provide our services and for our operational and business purposes.
